paper text.text:
For $n_c=n_e=2$, the construction gives $31{,}063$ candidates.
Of these, $26{,}502$ have a degree-three vertex with two adjacent
neighbors, contrary to Lemma~\ref{lem:independent-neighborhood}(a).
In a further $4{,}368$, some choice of the four twins gives a bridge
with four or five attachments~\supp{E29}. In each exclusion the
recorded degree-three vertex or the four chosen twins lie outside
$\{a,b,c,d,e\}$, so adding vertices on the original triples preserves
their neighborhoods. In the second case, the component containing
the old component outside the same $\Psi_3$ still has all its
original attachments.

The $193$ remaining candidates give $965$ cases over the five choices
of $(n_c,n_e)$. Of these, $172$ are toroidal and $782$ have a proper
nontoroidal minor. The other $11$ give the five graphs in the
statement up to isomorphism~\supp{E29}.

vertex names: Psi_3: twins p, q with neighbourhood {a,b,c} and r, z with neighbourhood {a,d,e}, as in Section 6. Further vertices with neighbourhood {a,b,c} are p3, p4, and with {a,d,e} r3, r4. Interior vertices of bridges are u0, u1, ... Vertices of the forms are B<k>_<x>; added single vertices are v_<neighbourhood>.
